approach: Add `check_part_coverage(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs as the last `step!` of `refusing_check`, so every earlier refusal keeps its name. A new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads a request's parts: runs of `(N)`, `N.`, `N)` and `(a)` lines at line start, plus bullets under an `Acceptance` heading. The runs numbered `N.` and `N)` are the form critic finding 1 said the parser missed. The parser skips quoted lines and fenced blocks. A run counts only if it numbers from 1 or a, has at least two entries, and each entry holds a distinctive stem. A new `stems` function (suffix strip, then trailing `e` strip, drops words under 3 letters, drops stop-list stems) feeds the matching. The stop set is built with the same stemmer, which is the fix for finding 2 on stem rules and the stop list. A part is covered when one acceptance criterion shares at least `min(n,2)` stems with it (n≤3) or `ceil(n/2)` (n≥4), so the three standard Steward bullets are covered by ordinary criteria. Only criteria count, not summary or out_of_scope, since a reading that defers a part names it there. The check is skipped for a decline or a question, and when the request itself allows a split (a sentence with `split`, `follow-up job`, `separately`, with no complaint cue such as said, wrong, earlier, reading, rejected). `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` stay as they are because `athena plan`, steward and hestia rely on them. The corpus gains refuse and accept cases for each input form, including a request rebuilt from the sza7 brief. The two corpus cases that pin the old `N)` and `(a)` gap are rewritten. A unit-test block, a declared-intent test and a CHANGELOG entry follow the pattern of the earlier checks. This finishes job 20261029-111202-2bpc, whose two major findings are fixed here. Job 20261029-084645-sza7's candidate files (athena.toml, checks.rs, disk.rs, run/mod.rs, CHANGELOG.md) stay dropped and are used only as test text.

decisions.choice: Put the parts parser in a new `request_parts` in topics.rs and leave `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` unchanged.
decisions.reason: `request_text_acceptance` feeds `athena plan` (topics.rs:411), steward.rs:587 and :1566, code_health.rs:1348 and hestia.rs:1781, and many tests assert its counts (hestia.rs:4089, :4393). Widening it would change plan acceptance everywhere. A separate parser meets finding 1 (N. and N) forms) with no unrelated behavior change. The corpus pins `bullets_expected` per case, and those counts stay put.

rejected.why: It changes plan acceptance, steward and hestia comparisons, and the pinned bullet counts. It breaks the 'no unrelated behavior changes' criterion.

decisions.choice: Add the step last in `refusing_check`, after `check_reading_references`.
decisions.reason: Every existing refusal keeps its name, because a corpus case that expects an earlier check still gets it first. The existing tests that assert step adjacency (outcome_state after governance, environment after outcome, history_fixture after survey) are untouched. The `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchor line (`step!(check_reading_references(`) stays valid.

rejected.option: Put it after `check_scope_limit` or near the criteria checks
rejected.why: It would shadow later checks in cases whose criteria differ from the request bullets, and it would change which check name existing Refuse cases report.

decisions.choice: A part is covered when one single criterion shares enough stems with it; only criteria text counts.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 speaks of a reading whose criteria cover the bullets. A deferring reading mentions the part in out_of_scope, assumptions or summary (the follow-up note), so counting that text would hide the deferral. One criterion at a time stops scattered incidental overlap from covering a part. Thresholds are min(n,2) for n≤3 stems and ceil(n/2) otherwise; the corpus fixes them.

rejected.option: Count the union of all reading text
rejected.why: The deferral note itself would cover the part.

rejected.option: Require every stem of the part
rejected.why: The Steward bullets are paraphrased by readers ('fails without the change and passes with it'), so a typical criterion would be refused. This is critic finding 2.

decisions.choice: One `stem` normaliser: lowercase, tokenise on non-alphanumerics, drop words under 3 letters, strip ing/ed/es/s/ly, then a trailing e. The stop set is the stop word list mapped through the same `stem` function.
decisions.reason: Without the trailing-e strip, change and changes give chang and change and never match. A stop list that is not stemmed the same way lets inflected function words through (others, afters). The list holds short and long function words (the, and, with, without, before, after, into, other, that, this, from, have, been).

rejected.option: Compare raw words, or stem the bullets only
rejected.why: This is the stem and stop-list order gap named in D148 and finding 2.

decisions.choice: Acceptance bullets count only under an `Acceptance` heading line (`Acceptance:`, `Acceptance criteria:`, or a markdown heading with that word). They run until the first non-blank line that is neither a bullet nor an indented continuation. Dash or star bullets with no such heading are not parts. Numbered and lettered runs count anywhere, outside quotes.
decisions.reason: The request text says 'any Acceptance bullet'. Plain dash lists such as 'Deliverable: ... - Add the default' (reading.rs:8445) and `complete_request` in drain.rs:6320 are not acceptance. Restricting limits how many existing fixtures are newly refused.

rejected.option: Treat every bullet from `request_text_acceptance` as a part
rejected.why: It would newly refuse evidence lists and context bullets, and every scripted reading in the CLI and run tests that has a one-line stock criterion.

decisions.choice: The split exemption is global to the request. A sentence (via the existing `sentences()` at checks.rs:332) holding a whole-word cue (`split`, `follow-up job`, `follow up job`, `separately`, `separate job`) exempts the request, unless the same sentence holds a whole-word complaint cue (said, wrong, earlier, reading, rejected). Matching uses `has_phrase` (surveys.rs:39) on lowercase text.
decisions.reason: This matches the brief and criterion 5. A complaint sentence that mentions a follow-up does not turn the deferral into permission.

rejected.why: The request rarely names the part in the same sentence, and a complaint cue needs a sentence scope anyway.

decisions.choice: Do not change READING_RULES in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs (so briefs.rs stays as it is) and do not edit any prompt file.
decisions.reason: The reader budget is 1998 of 2000 (docs/system-facts.md). Test `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` (briefs.rs:3493) fixes 11 rules (briefs.rs:3517) and a section under 3150 bytes (briefs.rs:3558). The refusal text is the reader's one correction and names the part and the repair. Criterion 8 makes the rules-text edit conditional, so it holds with no edit.

rejected.why: It breaks the budget test and the fixed rule count, and the brief forbids editing reader prompt files.

risks.risk: The rebuilt sza7 request text differs from the real one, because records/ is absent. I found no copy of the text in the snapshot (a search for sza7 matched nothing).

risks.risk: Stem overlap gives false coverage (a common stem such as test or pass covers an unrelated part), or false refusals when readers paraphrase.
risks.mitigation: A threshold of two shared stems for short parts and half the stems for longer ones. The stop set holds function words. Paired accept and refuse cases for the Steward bullets and the sza7 request fix the behavior; the producer tunes against these, not against fewer cases.

risks.risk: Existing fixtures with an `Acceptance:` heading and a stock criterion are newly refused (nested fake reader, scripted readings, steward and hestia generated requests). I did not enumerate them all; I read only the drain.rs, run/tests.rs and fake.rs hits.
risks.mitigation: Parts under a heading only, so plain dash lists are unaffected. The producer runs the whole `cargo test` and fixes a failing fixture's criteria (or the nested fake's reader_turn, the optional file above), never the production check.

risks.risk: A mid-line list such as 'do (1) x, (2) y, (3) z' in one paragraph is not read as parts (line start only).
risks.mitigation: Stated in the doc comment as a known miss. The sza7 request is rebuilt with the parts at line start; if the real one is a paragraph, a later change widens the parser.

risks.risk: The reader is not told about the new rule (reader rules and budget are unchanged), so the first reading may be refused and the second needs the refusal text.
risks.mitigation: The refusal message names each deferred part and the two repairs (cover it in a criterion, or the request allows a split). This is the same one-correction path the other checks use; the 5% estimate is declared.
